Hi Elena —

Following signature, attaching the version of the Mutual Action Plan (LB-MAP-v1.3.xlsx) that embeds the post-signature implementation workstreams: rollout windows, canary plan, data migration steps, and training schedule. Summary and asks below so the program team can confirm during the kickoff: 

High-level timeline (proposed):
- Week 1 (Jul 5–9): Knowledge transfer & environment provisioning (Customer env + test sandbox)
- Week 2 (Jul 12–16): Training sprint (trainer-led sessions + recorded modules)
- Week 3 (Jul 19–23): Canary pass (1% traffic; monitoring / smoke tests)
- Week 4 (Jul 26–30): Migration cutover & validation; fall back window Jul 31–Aug 2

Canary specifics (short):
- Canary window: 07/19 0200–07/23 20:00 PT
- Success criteria: <2% error rate vs. baseline, P95 latency within agreed SLO, no data loss on KV stores
- Rollback triggers: sustained >3% error for 10 minutes, model regression on eval suite, or critical customer-reported functional failures

Training & enablement:
- Two 60–90m live sessions (recorded) + an on-demand Q&A hour after each session
- Lab exercises in the sandbox (we'll share access tokens scoped to the program team)

Attachments included: LB-MAP-v1.3.xlsx (master MAP with task owners), training-schedule.ics (calendar stub). I'll also upload the canary runbook PDF once Jonas confirms monitoring hooks.

Asks for LumenBridge:
1) Confirm two trainer attendee slots (names/emails) by EOD Thu, Jun 17
2) Approve the proposed canary dates or propose an alternate week
3) Share your migration owner (primary + backup) so we can add them to the MAP and to the runbook

I'll sync with Marissa and Jonas on the operations cadence and monitoring deck before the kickoff. If this looks good, we'll lock calendar invites and final artifacts on Drive.

Thanks —

Elena — great, thanks for the quick reply and for naming Carlos. Written responses below and I've updated LB-MAP-v1.3 to add Carlos as migration owner and added granular tasks for data export validation (tab: Migration Tasks).

Short answers: 
- Canary health-check checklist (we'll add this to the runbook):
  • Synthetic end-to-end transaction success rate (compare to baseline)
  • Model output sanity checks (timeout, hallucination flags, tokenization errors)
  • KV cache hit-rate and spill-to-disk events
  • P95 latency; P99 alert threshold
  • Error budget burn rate > threshold

- Telemetry locations: we will publish a monitoring dashboard link (APM: NewRelic; logs in Splunk with a saved query name "LB_Canary_Health"). I'll paste direct links in the Drive runbook.

- Fallback SLA paragraph (for procurement):
  "During the agreed canary window, Redwood will maintain continuous monitoring and will execute an automated or manual rollback if canary health checks breach defined thresholds (sustained error rate above 3% for 10+ minutes, model regression on the acceptance eval, or a verified customer-facing functional failure). In the event of rollback, Redwood commits to a target recovery/rollback action within 30 minutes of confirmation and to coordinate a joint post-mortem within 48 hours. Critical data integrity incidents will trigger immediate rollback and customer notification."

Next steps (internal asks):
- Jonas: can you confirm monitoring hooks (NR alerts, Splunk saved queries) by EOD Thu, Jun 17?
- Marissa: please confirm trainer assignments and whether we should split the live sessions into East/West-friendly times.

I'll wait for Carlos/Ana confirmation and then publish calendar invites and the canary-runbook.pdf to Drive.

Thanks —
Olga
